answer: The anchor multiplier is published, charged in horizon, and zenith lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3937 identities would post 1286 proofs and burn roughly 42 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
